title: Scope chat transport and cancellation to a conversation

dependencies.reason: Implementation uses F-02 canonical lifecycle and workspace ownership. Owner authorized staged unmerged dependencies; this PR targets F-02.1 instead of main.

design.scope: Backend protocol only; no visible UI change

activation.readiness: initialized vault and running, non-draining agent; conversations capability must be enabled

behavior: Explicit conversation, turn and request IDs; durable monotonic conversation event sequences.
Canonical user/partial assistant persistence, transactional acceptance and exactly one terminal transition.
Conversation history, compaction and tool-exposure context; no scoped writes to shared primary history.
Only subscribed sockets receive scoped messages/progress; origin-only transient audio.
Cancellation reaches model and delegated-task signals, discards late chunks and cannot cancel newer turns.
Exact duplicate sends reconcile without generation; reconnect replays events and canonical messages.
Interrupted work becomes failed once on restart; no automatic execution replay.
Approval IDs retain a persisted originating turn across tab changes and restart.
Legacy stream/status mirroring remains behind a delivery adapter; opted-in sockets are excluded.

acceptance.check: Two interleaved fake model streams, tab switch and one cancel isolate text, progress, context and TTS
Duplicate sends, reconnect, restart and stale cancellation retain one terminal for the intended turn
Authenticated real WebSocket routing, disabled gate, legacy mirroring and stable approval identity
Unsafe subscriber broadcast, shared history and duplicate terminal mutations are detected

verification.note: New regressions on the reviewed implementation. All four failed at the relevant behavior assertion.
Includes existing workflow cancellation/authority, delegated approvals, sub-agent, browser-intent, taint and tool-filter tests. One existing platform-specific keychain skip.

quick_verify.expected: 30 tests pass across six files using isolated databases, authenticated fixture sockets, fake providers and shared cancellation primitives

migration: Four additive metadata tables and two indexes. Canonical conversation_messages remains the source of truth. Existing writers and history survive rollback; no table drops or destructive migration.
rollback: Unset JARVIS_BRIEF_CHAT_TRANSPORT and restart. Keep additive metadata, IDs and history; reconnect clients to the legacy protocol. Do not replay accepted effects.
limitations: No frontend cutover, draft/unread state, attachments, speech input migration or proactive speech changes.
Model and TTS are fixtures; no live credentials, paid evaluation, external effects or production data used.
Production scoped generation concurrency is one; fake tests alone use concurrency two.
Speech synthesis starts after full text and is not replayed on reconnect; providers may take time to release an aborted iterator.
Cancellation does not undo completed effects or revoke canonical approval requests.
Replay pages have count/byte bounds; current snapshot messages must not receive old replay deltas twice. Older messages use the F-02 history endpoint.
The daemon remains a single authenticated owner; workspace guards do not create a multi-tenant auth system.
The main update from PR #716 changes approval label helpers separately from this routing patch; preserve it when rebasing the stack.
